issues.title: Resolve the full-profile recovery gap against accepted configuration-only backups
issues.architecture: Decision-only task. Preserve ADR-0008 until the user explicitly accepts a superseding or extending ADR. No new snapshot format, scheduler, migration or encryption code in this slice.
criteria: Inventory local drafts/attachments, linked tasks, labels, settings, keys, accounts and cache; identify which data can actually be reconstructed from each provider and which cannot.

Reuse existing ADR-0008/#54 tests and evidence for configuration-only restore in a disposable synthetic profile; add only missing corruption, wrong-passphrase and partial-failure coverage. Do not touch user profiles or claim those tests establish full-profile recovery.
Present options retaining configuration-only recovery versus adding a consistent full-profile snapshot, including cost, privacy, compatibility, encryption, retention and failure handling.
Record the human decision before implementation follow-ups. If configuration-only remains chosen, keep full-backup parity explicitly unmet rather than closing #113 as delivered.
After approval, split snapshot/restore from scheduling and multi-profile work; discovery and single-profile recovery must not wait on all of #99.
executionPrerequisites: Final decision: maintainer approval of the concrete recovery options
issues.evidence: Planning only on 2026-10-05; no implementation/native/provider acceptance claimed.

issues.title: Validate Windows install, update and recovery on an exact-SHA candidate
issues.areas: Windows validation workflow; NSIS; updater; native test harness; artifact manifest
issues.architecture: Keep staged user-confirmed updates and existing packaging under ADR-0008. Signing/authenticity or rollback-policy changes require approval; validation does not publish a release.
criteria: Build through the CI-only validation workflow; bind canonical executable/installer hashes and all evidence to the same source SHA. Do not reuse an old green commit for changed source.
Use clean disposable Windows environments and synthetic prior-version profiles to test install, startup/restart, upgrade, locked executable/unsaved work and interrupted update recovery.

Test uninstall behavior explicitly: preserve user data unless deletion was explicitly selected; document supported downgrade limits instead of promising backward-compatible profile opening. Verify whether failed updates leave a usable installation and recoverable profile; record any gap instead of promising an unimplemented rollback.
Cover native mail reader/composer, DPI/zoom/IME, mailto, notifications and suspend/reconnect where available; onboarding-only screenshots do not certify those workflows.

Verify artifacts before replacement; retire only superseded binaries under AGENTS.md. Record signing/authenticity and provider gaps separately; final product acceptance still needs #53/#54 and the chosen recovery contract.
executionPrerequisites: Candidate build: seven successful required main CI jobs for its exact SHA

issues.title: Measure native mailbox responsiveness and memory with the existing 1k/10k/100k datasets
issues.areas: scripts/perf; native Windows harness; mailbox/reader/attachment flows; docs/performance-baseline.md
issues.architecture: Reuse current datasets/runtime. Review any benchmark dependency under existing policy; request approval only for architecture changes, external services/cost or conflicts with accepted decisions. Do not introduce a new virtualization or storage architecture merely to improve a benchmark.
criteria: Record device, OS, app/engine versions, SHA, dataset hash, cache state and repetitions; isolate local interaction time from provider latency.
Measure startup, cached first-page, downloaded-message open, search interaction, scrolling and repeated message/PDF memory cycles for 1k/10k/100k datasets.
Calibrate proposed p95 targets from #53 (100ms local reaction, 500ms cached first page, 300ms downloaded-message open); publish observed results and accepted budgets rather than fabricated promises.
Compare baseline/candidate using the same visible data and account for warmup/noise; do not hide messages or reduce functionality to pass.
Record actionable regressions and add suitable repeatable checks; synthetic algorithm results and shared-runner timing alone cannot certify native responsiveness.
executionPrerequisites: Native evidence: available reference Windows device and exact-SHA test build

issues.title: Make settings and command actions discoverable, localized and keyboard-accessible
issues.areas: frontend/src/components/dialog/SettingsDialog.tsx; command palette; locales; existing settings state
issues.architecture: Reuse existing settings, command actions and components. No new command engine, persistence model or parallel design system.
criteria: Inventory existing sections/commands before changes; provide localized search/navigation to existing appearance, signature, account, privacy and update controls without duplicating their state.

Initial slice: localized English/Spanish command names, hints and searchable synonyms; preserve existing fallback contracts for other catalogs and leave full localization acceptance under #37. Distinguish commands from settings results. Test accents and non-ASCII queries so unsupported normalization cannot match every command.
Search and activate using keyboard, restore focus after closing/navigating, preserve unsaved settings and show a clear empty result.
Keep account context and capability restrictions when invoking actions; finding a command never grants permission or sends a message automatically.
Cover light/dark, long Spanish labels, narrow panes, 200% zoom, focus return and persistence with automated production-entry tests and applicable native evidence.
issues.evidence: Planning only on 2026-10-05; no implementation/native/provider acceptance claimed.

issues.title: Expose per-account sync health and accessible recovery without losing errors
issues.areas: frontend/src/states/connectivity.ts; ConnectivityBanner; account navigation; existing sync events
issues.architecture: Present existing signals and reuse existing recovery commands. First inventory backend observability; missing signals must remain unknown. A new sync engine, durable queue or health persistence model needs approval.
criteria: Inventory and display known per-account states: syncing, last successful sync where observable, offline, authentication required, failed and unavailable/unknown; never infer full mailbox freshness from a partial folder sync.

Two concurrent account errors remain distinguishable; dismissing a notice does not falsely make that account healthy or clear another account's condition. A successful unrelated service/folder cannot clear a known failure; if events lack that scope, retain unknown/degraded rather than claiming complete health. Do not invent a staleness threshold.
Offer account-scoped retry/reconnect using existing commands; do not retry uncertain sends or start unsupported Graph writes as part of recovery.
Retain readable actionable copy and accessible announcements without stealing focus or repeatedly interrupting reading; preserve redaction of credentials and diagnostic details.
Test simultaneous failures, account switching/removal, late responses, retry success/failure and revoked consent with light/dark/narrow/keyboard evidence; disclose limits of session-only state.
